skill.name: figma
skill.description: Import Figma assets, tokens, components, storyboard frames, motion, and shader exports into HyperFrames compositions using CLI and MCP workflows.
skill.summary: Bring Figma design assets and motion into HyperFrames video compositions.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown inline examples rather than executable code. Confirmed risks are the intended HyperFrames CLI and npx workflows. The report also flags project .env token guidance; no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill directs agents to run HyperFrames CLI commands against user-provided Figma references.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running commands, validate Figma references, and run only in trusted projects.

remediation.issue: The skill suggests persisting FIGMA_TOKEN in a shell profile or project .env file.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend secure local secret storage, add .env to ignore rules, and avoid storing tokens in shared project files.

remediation.issue: The validation step uses npx, which may execute project or package code.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a pinned local HyperFrames dependency and tell users before running package-managed commands.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable ways to move Figma work into video compositions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through HyperFrames imports for assets, tokens, components, motion, and storyboards.
actual_capabilities: Routes Figma links to asset, token, component, motion, shader, or storyboard workflows.
Guides static asset exports through the HyperFrames Figma CLI with local frozen files.
Imports brand variables and published styles into HyperFrames composition variables.
Converts Figma node trees into editable HyperFrames HTML components.
Uses Figma MCP motion context to build GSAP timeline scripts when REST cannot provide motion data.
Explains storyboard parsing so frame strips become animated element timelines.
limitations: Requires a Figma personal access token with read-only scopes for REST-based imports.
Motion and shader workflows depend on a separate authenticated Figma MCP connector.
Figma variables may require Enterprise access, with published styles used as fallback.
Shader rendering is mostly manual because Figma MCP rendering flattens shader output.

use_cases.title: Import Brand Assets
use_cases.description: Turn Figma logos, icons, and visual assets into local HyperFrames media with provenance and alt text.

use_cases.title: Build Editable Scenes
use_cases.description: Convert a Figma frame into editable HyperFrames HTML while preserving geometry and token bindings.

use_cases.title: Create Storyboard Animatics
use_cases.description: Parse a Figma section of scene frames into animated timelines instead of flat slide sequences.

prompt_templates.title: Import One Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Figma link to import the selected logo into my HyperFrames composition. Prefer SVG and describe where the frozen file lands.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Brand Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Import the brand tokens from this Figma file and explain which values became composition variables and which values used fallbacks.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Figma frame into an editable HyperFrames component. Link imported tokens when possible and list unresolved bindings.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Storyboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Figma section as storyboard keyframes. Build element timelines from matching objects and explain any still-frame fallbacks.

output_examples.input: A user provides a Figma logo frame and asks to use it in a composition.
output: The assistant verifies that Figma read access is configured.
It imports the logo as a frozen local media asset.
It reports the asset location, description, and next preview step.

output_examples.input: A user asks to recreate a Figma hero frame as an editable scene.
output: The assistant imports brand tokens first when available.
It converts the frame into a HyperFrames component.
It identifies linked tokens and any unresolved library references.

output_examples.input: A user provides a Figma storyboard section with motion notes below the frames.
output: The assistant treats frames as keyframes, not slides.
It groups matching elements across frames and plans transitions.
It explains which scenes remain stills and why.

best_practices: Import tokens before components so colors and styles can bind to brand variables.
Freeze all Figma assets locally before rendering a composition.
Tell the user which credential each phase needs before running a workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not leave live Figma URLs inside rendered compositions.
Do not guess missing token libraries or match tokens by color value alone.
Do not treat storyboard frames as simple slides when elements can animate between states.

faq.question: What does this skill import from Figma?
faq.answer: It covers assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard sections, motion context, and shader export guidance for HyperFrames compositions.

faq.question: Does it write changes back to Figma?
faq.answer: No. The documented Figma token scopes are read-only, and imports create local HyperFrames artifacts.

faq.question: Why does motion require MCP?
faq.answer: Figma REST does not expose equivalent motion data, so the skill uses the Figma MCP connector for motion context.

faq.question: Can it import Figma variables on every plan?
faq.answer: No. Figma variables can require Enterprise access, and the skill falls back to published styles when needed.

faq.question: How does it keep renders deterministic?
faq.answer: It freezes imported assets locally and records provenance so renders do not depend on live Figma requests.

faq.question: Is this safe to use with private Figma files?
faq.answer: Use read-only credentials, confirm commands before running them, and keep tokens out of shared project files.
